key_insight: Symmetry-based low-rank fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M enables accurate lattice thermal conductivity predictions across compounds sharing a crystal symmetry without fine-tuning each compound separately.
engineering_relevance: Faster thermal conductivity screening could support thermal management and materials selection for photovoltaic, microelectronic, and thermoelectric applications.
method: Select a small set of compounds sharing a crystal symmetry.
Fine-tune MatterSim 1M using symmetry-based few-shot low-rank adaptation.
Predict lattice thermal conductivity by solving the Boltzmann transport equation.
evidence_signal: Across half-Heuslers (space group 216), space-group-225 materials, and spinels (227), the method reduced mean absolute relative differences from reference calculations by 2–3× versus untuned MatterSim 1M, with accuracy comparable to per-compound fine-tuning and approximately 5–7× lower fine-tuning time for 100 compounds.
watch_item: Transfer was demonstrated within shared-symmetry groups; generalization to other symmetries or improved solar-cell device performance was not established.
paper_title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
